mathematical_or_operational_scope: Independent exact n=8 dual-chart reconstruction over Z[z]/(z^4+1), general-size modular onion checks, and an eight-variable rational-circuit exporter. Supports chart identities and guarded partial candidates, not a full Fourier factorization.
positive_controls: Lines 97–142 reconstruct all dual equations and require exact variable order, shuffle, unique names, all coefficients, and complete equation-name coverage.
Lines 188–221 use modular inverses and independent 2x2 solves for chart denominators; lines 298–307 export determinant, corner, gap and denominator-related guards.

Lines 328,351–365,395–415 compare coefficient factor removal, cleared-column scaling, direct matrices, rational circuits and corner conditions. Lines 419–443 distinguish a partial exception witness from a factorization.

findings.issue: The reference residual loop checks only entries supplied by ref[residuals]. An empty residual list passes, while the report says all_twelve_values_match=True. There is no length, uniqueness or exact-name-set test for these twelve claimed values.

ZIP members are indexed by basename with silent last-writer-wins collisions; no duplicate-basename, expansion or depth guard is imposed here. Manifest presence is required by lookup, but an empty manifest verifies zero entries and reports all_match=True.

Externally supplied modulus/root and witness shapes are trusted. The verifier does not validate primality, exact root order or coefficient-field embedding for these loaded witnesses; hard-coded test primes/root constructors are a separate, safer path.
Random circuit checks skip every denominator exception and require no minimum successful count. The fixed reference remains a check, but the fresh-comparison report is not a coverage guarantee.
required_nonzero and inverse operands are emitted as a contract rather than enforced against a newly supplied solution. Empty exception-witness data passes without a required count.
Proof/check acceptance relies on assertions, removable under optimized Python. Output files are written during the audit before all checks finish.

cost_and_scaling: Sparse polynomial multiplication is quadratic in operand term counts plus monomial sorting. Direct modular Fourier products and inversion cost O(n^3) field operations and O(n^2) storage. The generic determinant circuit uses subset dynamic programming with O(n·2^n) transitions, although exported n is fixed at 8. This is not a sub-FFT algorithm or growing-n factorization construction.
test_scope_and_limits: Designed tests: 12 usable dual samples for each of 3 primes and 4 primitive eighth roots (144 samples); 8 usable onion samples for each of 13 size/prime pairs (104); up to 90 random rational-circuit comparisons plus a fixed reference; source-provided exceptional samples. These tests were read, not run. General-size claims still require the support proof beyond finitely many checks.
certificate_acceptance: Exact coefficient equality for the complete dual export is meaningfully checked. The onion circuit and reference residual labels need independent schema/completeness validation; feasibility requires every residual and guard, not just selected identities or a nonzero modular witness.
